title: The Value of Curiosity
text:
Curiosity is an abstract noun that describes a strong desire to learn or understand something. Researchers often argue that curiosity drives scientific progress, because it encourages people to question established assumptions. However, the willingness to explore unfamiliar ideas is not evenly distributed across societies. Some educational systems reward obedience more than inquiry, which can suppress this disposition.

Psychologists have found that curiosity can be cultivated through deliberate practice. Teachers who ask open-ended questions tend to produce students who display greater persistence when faced with difficult problems. Consequently, the ability to tolerate uncertainty is increasingly regarded as an essential academic skill. Such findings suggest that curiosity is not merely a personal trait but a quality that institutions can deliberately nurture.

questions.text: According to paragraph one, what does curiosity describe?
options: A strong desire to learn or understand something

questions.text: According to paragraph two, what do teachers who ask open-ended questions tend to produce?
options: Students who are less interested in learning
Students who show greater persistence with difficult problems

questions.text: What can be inferred about educational systems that reward obedience more than inquiry?
options: They are likely to discourage curiosity
They always produce the most successful scientists
They encourage students to challenge assumptions
They have no effect on students' behaviour

questions.text: What does the author imply about the role of institutions in developing curiosity?
options: They have little influence on curiosity
They can help develop curiosity deliberately
They are responsible only for personal traits

things taken to be true without proof
developed or improved through practice and care
the quality of continuing firmly despite difficulties

paragraph_translations: Merak, bir şeyi öğrenme veya anlama konusunda güçlü bir istek anlamına gelen soyut bir isimdir. Araştırmacılar genellikle merakın bilimsel ilerlemeyi yönlendirdiğini savunur, çünkü insanları yerleşik varsayımları sorgulamaya teşvik eder. Ancak yabancı fikirleri keşfetme isteği toplumlar arasında eşit dağılmamıştır. Bazı eğitim sistemleri sorgulamadan çok itaati ödüllendirir, bu da bu eğilimi bastırabilir.

Psikologlar merakın bilinçli bir uygulamayla geliştirilebileceğini bulmuşlardır. Açık uçlu sorular soran öğretmenler, zorlu problemlerle karşılaştıklarında daha fazla azim gösteren öğrenciler yetiştirme eğilimindedir. Sonuç olarak belirsizliğe tahammül etme becerisi giderek temel bir akademik beceri olarak görülmektedir. Bu bulgular, merakın yalnızca kişisel bir özellik değil, kurumların bilinçli olarak besleyebileceği bir nitelik olduğunu göstermektedir.
